utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm Dr. Rao. Thanks for coming in — I've got about 15 minutes for you today. The booking says you've had burning when you wee since yesterday and you're wondering if it's a UTI again. Can you tell me about it from the start?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so about a day and a half ago. It really stings and burns, especially right at the end, just like my last UTI. I am going constantly, about every half hour, and only a little bit comes out so I always have to rush. It is a bit cloudy and smells, but I have not seen any blood.

utterance:
That does sound like typical cystitis symptoms. Let me ask a few important screening questions.
1) Have you had any fever, chills, back pain under your ribs, or feeling generally unwell or sick to your stomach?
2) Any pain low down in your tummy (above your pubic bone)?
3) Have you had any vaginal itching or any unusual discharge?
4) When was your last period, and have you been on the pill regularly — any chance you could be pregnant?
reply: Sorry, that's a lot of questions at once. Could you ask me one thing at a time?

utterance: Sorry, that's a lot of questions at once. Let me take it one at a time. First: have you had any fever, shivers, or pain up in your back under the ribs?
reply: No, I haven't had any fevers or shivers, and there's nothing in my back. I just have a bit of an ache low down in my tummy, but otherwise I feel fine apart from this.

utterance: Good — that's reassuring, so this doesn't sound like a kidney infection. Do you have any vaginal itching or any unusual discharge?
Thanks. To make sure I'm not missing a different cause: have you started seeing a new partner recently, and do you usually use condoms?
reply: Um, yeah, I have a boyfriend; we have been together about a year and it is just him, and we do not use condoms because I am on the pill.

utterance: When you say "again" — how many times have you had these UTI symptoms before, and did you ever have a urine test done for any of them?
reply: I had one UTI about two years ago, that is it.

finding: Soft abdomen. Mild suprapubic tenderness. No guarding or rebound. No masses.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

utterance: I'm going to test your urine with a dipstick — it takes a second and confirms what we're thinking. It also checks for blood and any other surprises.
reply: Do I really need to do a test? I've got to get back to work at the café soon.

utterance: It's worth two minutes for a couple of reasons: it confirms it really is a bladder infection so we don't give you antibiotics for nothing, and it checks for blood in the urine, which — even when you can't see it — can point to something else. If it looks good, you're done and back to the café in a couple of minutes. I'll only do a sample; no culture unless the test says we need one. Fair enough?
reply: Fair enough, let's just get it done quickly then.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance:
Here's your plan. You've got a classic, uncomplicated bladder infection — it's very common and very treatable.

Medication: I've prescribed nitrofurantoin, 100 mg, one capsule twice a day for 5 days. Please take it with food. It's not a "take until you feel better" medicine — finish all 5 days even if you feel fine after a day or two, so the infection is fully cleared and doesn't come back. It doesn't interfere with your pill.

Comfort: The stinging should start easing within a day or two. You can take paracetamol or ibuprofen for the burning and ache, and drink plenty of water. Don't hold your wee for long.

When to come back — this part matters:
- If you develop a fever, shivering, pain in your back under the ribs, or you feel generally unwell or vomiting, that could mean the infection has spread to the kidneys — come back or call us the same day.
- If you're not obviously better after about 48 hours, or if the burning comes back once you finish the course, come back and we'll do a urine culture to make sure we've targeted the right bug.

If you get these infections more than a couple of times a year from now, let us know — we'd want a culture and to talk about prevention, because the approach changes.

Does that all make sense, and do you have any questions before you head back to the café?
reply: That all makes sense, thank you. I will just grab the script and head straight back to the café.
